```{r, echo = FALSE, message=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
# plotly.js from the CDN, so the site's pages don't each copy it
options(plotly.core.plotlyjs = "cdn")
```

CSV or comma-delimited-values is a very popular format for storing structured data. In this tutorial, we will see how to plot beautiful graphs using csv data. We will learn how to import csv data from an external source (a URL), and plot it using Plotly.

First we import the data and look at it.

```{r}
data <- read.csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/2014_apple_stock.csv')
head(data)
```

### Plot from CSV with Plotly

```{r}
library(plotly.core)

data <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/2014_apple_stock.csv")

fig <- go_figure() |>
  add_scatter(
    x = as.Date(data$AAPL_x),
    y = data$AAPL_y,
    mode = "lines",
    name = "Share Prices (in USD)"
  ) |>
  update_layout(
    title = "Apple Share Prices over time (2014)",
    plot_bgcolor = "#e5ecf6",
    xaxis = go_xaxis(
      title = "AAPL_x",
      zerolinecolor = "#ffff",
      zerolinewidth = 2,
      gridcolor = "ffff"
    ),
    yaxis = go_yaxis(
      title = "AAPL_y",
      zerolinecolor = "#ffff",
      zerolinewidth = 2,
      gridcolor = "ffff"
    ),
    showlegend = TRUE,
    width = 1100
  )

fig
```
